caveats.common: Every family: a top-down 4-DoF wrist (no roll or pitch), open-loop timing, no perception (the placement error is unknown to the controller), soft contacts and a 1 ms timestep. The recommendation is a simulation ranking under these conditions, not a hardware guarantee. The jaw's registration reference is its centre line; every other family's is repeatability against its own nominal episode, and each family runs at its own declared actuation limits.
caveats.catalog_gripper: Rigid models with the upstream actuator limits; the adaptive grippers are our own geometry. Scripted closing, no tactile feedback.
caveats.catalog_hand: Simplified rigid models with no skin compliance, driven by scripted open-to-closed synergies: no tactile feedback, no regrasp. Actuator limits are the upstream model's. Rubber pads would grip better than the part's mu 0.3 used here, so results are conservative for padded hands.
caveats.designed: Rigid models generated from a recipe and driven by scripted synergies. The random control from the same space is shown beside the Nemotron designs; no superiority is claimed.
caveats.parallel_jaw: The core experiment's own scene, checks and scorer. Registration is measured against the jaw's centre line.
caveats.soft_arm: Approximation: a chain of rigid capsules with spring-damper joints, curled by a tension-limited cable. Not modelled: continuum mechanics, material non-linearity, suckers. Verify on hardware.
caveats.suction: Approximation: the seal is a geometric test gating an adhesion actuator capped at vacuum times lip area. Not modelled: air flow, leaks, porosity, vacuum build-up time, lip hysteresis. Treat as a screen, then verify on hardware.

rules.eligible: certified; nominal test passes the requirement; no physics_invalid episode; nominal not physics_unreliable
rules.rank: certificate score, then the smaller placement tolerance, then screen success
rules.simplicity: fewer actuators, then lower mass, then higher fidelity (core, rigid, approximation)
rules.fidelity: an approximation winner carries the best core or rigid candidate as runner-up
